title: Fatigue in Parkinson's
content: Fatigue is a common non-movement symptom experienced by some people with Parkinson's disease. A person may describe feeling very tired, exhausted, drained, physically tired, mentally tired, having very little energy, or feeling tired throughout the day even after resting. Fatigue can make everyday tasks feel more difficult and is different from simply feeling sleepy, although sleep problems may contribute. Depression, medications, physical inactivity and other medical conditions can also contribute to fatigue. Feeling tired or exhausted does not by itself indicate Parkinson's disease. Persistent, unexplained or significant fatigue should be discussed with a healthcare professional so that possible causes can be evaluated.
